keyFindings.description: The change takes the skill body to 501 lines (net +2), over the repository's own 500-line guard, so `packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts`'s `every skill body stays under 500 lines` fails and the `pi-legion` CI check is red at code head a5e26319624d. Reproduced in the workspace: `bun test packages/pi-legion/src/skills-guard.test.ts` → `(fail) … [{file: legion-worker/SKILL.md, lines: 501}]`. `longSkillBodies` counts `split("\n").length`, so a 500-newline file is 501. Move the added text into a reference or shorten it.

The change's own live proof cannot start. The Stage 4a marker is `ompSessionsDir + "/" + SandboxName(token) + ".marker"`, and this change deletes the mount that made that path exist (`manifest.go`: the role containers lost `{Name: issueVolume, MountPath: ompSessionsDir, SubPath: SessionsSubPath}`) and drops `ompSessionsDir` from `legionMountPaths()`. The live Stage 4a run against b650d854 (image sha-a5e26319624d) failed at `root-ready` with `stage4a-setup: 107: cannot create /home/legion/.omp/profiles/legion/agent/sessions/<sandbox>.marker: Directory nonexistent`, `runtime.kubernetes.setup exited 2`; `suspend`, `cleanup-reaps-the-issue`, `issue-suspend-resume`, `re-adopt`, `secrets-old-uid-and-revocation`, `displaced` and `kill-launcher` never ran. Move the marker to `TreeRoot`, which every role container still mounts read-write and which dies with the pod — the property the rig now claims. Audited: no live check asserts the marker surviving across pods, so no assertion changes with it.

`released_msg="sandbox runtime: released the closed issue's Sandbox and the volume it owned"` is a log line nothing writes any more: `internal/runtime/sandbox/issue_suspend.go:63` now logs `sandbox runtime: deleted the closed issue's Sandbox and the role Secrets it owned`. `released_lines` (`:3614`) finds none, so the `child-release` check fails at `:3634` (`want once`). The unit test was updated (`internal/daemon/outbox_issue_suspend_test.go:671`); the harness was not.

Four assertions require a parked or check-suspended issue to keep one Sandbox in `Suspended` mode (`:3645` `child2_parked`, `:4835`, `:6174`, `:6176`). `SuspendIssue` now deletes the Sandbox unconditionally after `awaitPodGone` (`issue_suspend.go:57-63`), and the park path reaches it exactly as the close path does (`internal/workflow/linger.go:74-96` enqueues `record.IssueSuspend` for any non-done, non-merged stop → `internal/daemon/outbox.go:455-466`). `issue_sandbox_modes` then prints nothing: `:4835`, `:6174` and `:6176` fail deterministically and `:3645` burns its 600 s `until_true`. The delete is the intended design, so the harness is what is wrong.

The cutover charges deaths to roles the daemon itself ended. `suspendDisplacing` writes `legion.dev/displaced-pod` on the Sandbox (`relaunch.go:141`, `:857`), then `replaceSupersededSandbox` deletes that Sandbox and creates a new one from `sandboxManifest`, whose `ObjectMeta` carries `Labels` and no annotations (`manifest.go:352-359`). `displaced()` reads only that annotation (`observe.go:132-137`, `:146-151`), and `evaluate` re-reads the Sandbox from the API server (`observe.go:92-102`), so the re-read finds nothing or the annotation-free replacement. The supervisor then takes `died` rather than `displaced` (`supervise/machine.go:1111-1115`), interrupting the turn and charging a death. `migrate` is true for every issue Sandbox of the previous release (`supersededDisk`, `relaunch.go:529-532`) and `live` is the common upgrade case, so the five other roles of each running issue are charged on the one path the whole feature routes through. Carry the predecessor's uid onto the replacement.

`ends()` widened from `!obs.WorkspaceLost` (exit code 3 of one named init container) to `!obs.InitFailed` (any non-zero init termination, `observe.go:185`, and `failedInit` also reads `LastTerminationState`, `:336-349`). `relaunch` treats a pod still inside its init containers as `live` (`relaunch.go:120`), so such a pod can be displaced; the kubelet then kills its running init container during the delete, `InitFailed` is true, `ends()` is false, `displaced()` cannot fire and the supervisor charges a death. `implement.json` claims the widening changes no observable behaviour because the annotation is written only for a live pod — a pod in init is live. `InitFailed = initExit != nil && pod.DeletionTimestamp == nil` keeps the init-keeps-failing behaviour the field exists for.

The postgres-only cutover is enforced in `config/kubernetes.go:1120-1127` and nowhere else: `configure` never refuses an empty `SessionDSNKey`, so the whole file-session mode is still carried by the runtime — `manifest.go:565` (`providers()` returning no Secret), `:575`, `:587`, `:594`, `:605`, `:901`, `operatorpod.go:169` — and `types.go:146-153` still documents `""` as "keeps each session a file in the issue's volume's sessions directory … no launch expects the issue's volume to hold a session". What those branches implement is precisely the failure the new refusal exists to prevent, and acceptance 5 asks that no such code be left. Refuse `""` in `configure` and delete the branches; `mountsProviders()` goes with them.

`workspaceInit` still creates `<root>/sessions` on every issue pod's disk, as a bare `"sessions"` literal, and nothing mounts or reads it: the role containers' `{issueVolume, ompSessionsDir, SessionsSubPath}` mount is deleted in this change, and the only surviving `SessionsSubPath` reader is `SessionOnVolume` (`manifest.go:284-297`), whose one caller is `legion sessions import --tree-volume` reading a legion-v10.0.0 tree volume mounted elsewhere. Delete the `MkdirAll`, its error path, the assertion at `workspace_init_test.go:467` and the two comments that still call it "the sessions directory the main container mounts" (`workspace_init.go:137`, `workspace_init_test.go:432`).

Step 1 of the cutover runbook tells the operator to find the issues still to cut over by the boot line `sandbox runtime: issue Sandbox <name> owns an "issue" claim template, …`. The daemon logs a different message, with the name as a structured attribute: `install.go:146-147`, `sandbox runtime: the issue Sandbox owns a claim template, the disk shape before the pod-owned disk; its next launch replaces it`, `"sandbox", object.GetName()`. The step finds nothing, so an operator concludes there is nothing to cut over and skips step 2, whose point is that unpushed work is lost at the next launch.

Operator documentation still teaches machinery this change deleted, in the file the change rewrote 802 lines of: `:1553-1556` lists the boot refusals as `session_store` other than `pvc` or `postgres` and a `session_dsn_secret` under `pvc`; `:3647` shows `session_store: pvc # default` in a configuration example that now fails config load; `:4083` teaches `LEGION_RESUME_SESSION_FILE`, which exists nowhere in the code; `:4334` and `:4433` teach `workspace-init controller` exiting 3 as a lost volume, and no exit 3 exists. `:1065`, `:771` and `:2154` still describe sessions living on the volume.

No `## Contract change census`. The change adds a refusal (`session_store` must be `postgres`), makes a field required (`session_dsn_secret`), removes fields (`record.IssueSuspend.Release`, `store.IssueClose.Release`, `Observation.WorkspaceLost`, `SpawnSpec.WorkspaceRecoveredFrom`), changes a signature at a package boundary (`runtime.IssueSuspender.SuspendIssue` loses `release bool`), removes an environment variable (`LEGION_EXPECT_ISSUE_VOLUME`) and a CLI subcommand (`legion sessions mark-lost`), and raises the daemon/plugin contract to 36. The census, its search commands re-run at the head, and a disposition for every hit are required.

Security[sandbox]: with `pvc` refused, every deployment keeps every issue's, role's and tree's transcript in one database whose URL is projected into the providers Secret (`manifest.go:575-581`), mounted on every role container (`:437`) and named to the agent as `OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE` (`:901-904`); the table is keyed by session path with no tenant column. A Legion agent reads untrusted text by design, so one that follows injected text can read and rewrite another role's or tree's history, which that session's next resume feeds back to its agent (OWASP LLM01, LLM06). Under the `pvc` mode this change deletes, sessions were on a disk no other issue's pod could mount. State the trust assumption in "Selecting the store"; narrowing the session login is the architect's decision, raised to it in this round.

`treeVolumeLayout` now returns no refusal for an issue Sandbox with zero claim templates. A child Sandbox of the tree-volume layout is exactly that shape, so it is adopted silently where it was refused `owns no volume`, losing the fence that forced the drained cutover `docs/kubernetes.md` still prescribes. Only the root's `tree` template and the old controller still trip it.

The migration's selection is exact, but nothing fences it against the previous release still writing. The only lock is the migration advisory lock (`store/store.go:183-187`); the docs say the earlier release's pods keep running through a rollout (`docs/kubernetes.md:989`), and a child closing as done during the overlap enqueues `{"release":true}` after the strip, which the new daemon's strict decode then stalls on — the exact failure the migration prevents. The pvc→postgres runbook scales the daemon to 0 (`docs/kubernetes.md:664-666`); the pod-owned-disk cutover says only "once the image is applied" (`:1112`). Say the earlier daemon is scaled to 0 first.

`Observation.InitFailed` sits on the cross-runtime observation contract with no consumer outside the package that writes it (`sandbox/observe.go:127,185` and sandbox tests only); `WorkspaceLost` earned its place because `supervise.Machine.died` read it, and that reader is gone. `relaunch.go:191-193` still says supervision observes a Gone "which carries InitFailed", which supervision never looks at. Keep the classification inside the package.

`lost_detail` and the `pod_watch_verdict` arm that exempts it (`:1659-1670`) are dead scaffolding kept with a comment saying nothing writes it any more, pinned by a unit test (`scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts:904`). Delete the variable, the exemption and the test's parameter.

Prose the sweep left behind, each now false: `names.go:15-16` ("sessions stay on it") and `:44-45`; `manifest.go:677-678`; `sandbox.go:10` ("retaining the volume and sessions until linger cleanup") and `:823-824` ("keeps its uid, volume and sessions"); `operatorpod.go:19-20`; `podsafety/podsafety.go:11-12`.

`claimTemplates` and `diskSource` split one decision — who owns this pod's disk — into two methods that must agree out of band with the controller's template name `issue` and its claim name `IssueClaimName` (`:307-318`). One method returning both would keep the invariant in one place. Not blocking; the kind-dispatch design is otherwise right.

thermonuclear.deepReview: CHANGES — the superseded-Sandbox replacement losing the displaced-pod annotation; Security[sandbox] on the one shared session store; the cutover runbook's census line; stale docs; the census no longer refusing a templateless issue Sandbox; migration 0051 unfenced against the previous release.
